title: Prototypes, Object Delegation & ES6 Class Systems
summary: Master the prototype chain, [[Prototype]] vs .prototype, Object.create, and ES6 class syntax with private fields and inheritance.
learningObjectives: Explain prototypal inheritance and lookup resolution along the [[Prototype]] chain
Implement secure, encapsulated ES6 classes utilizing native private fields (#field) and inheritance

sections.heading: 1. The Prototype Chain & Behavior Delegation Mechanics
sections.content:
Unlike traditional class-based languages (Java, C++) where classes are blueprints that copy methods into instances upon creation, JavaScript uses Behavior Delegation through Prototypes.

Key Concepts:
- `[[Prototype]]`: An internal hidden slot on every JavaScript object pointing to another object (its prototype).
- `Object.prototype`: The root of the prototype chain. Its prototype is `null`.
- Property Lookup: When accessing `obj.prop`, V8 checks `obj` directly. If not found, it checks `obj.[[Prototype]]`, then `obj.[[Prototype]].[[Prototype]]`, continuing up the chain until it finds the property or reaches `null` (returning `undefined`).
- Function `.prototype`: Every standard function has a public `.prototype` property. When invoked with `new Constructor()`, the newly created object's `[[Prototype]]` is set to `Constructor.prototype`.

ES6 Classes:
ES6 `class` syntax is syntactic sugar over prototype delegation, providing cleaner structure while preserving prototypal inheritance:
- Methods defined on the class body are attached to `ClassName.prototype` (shared across all instances in memory).
- Private fields (`#privateField`) are enforced natively by V8 at the engine level; they cannot be accessed or overridden from outside the class.

codeExamples.explanation: Property lookups traverse the [[Prototype]] chain until a matching property is found or null is reached.

keyPoints: JavaScript objects inherit through prototype references, sharing methods without duplicating them in memory.
ES6 classes provide clean syntax for constructors, super calls, and native private fields (#).
Mutating prototypes at runtime slows down V8 optimizations by breaking hidden classes.
commonMistakes: Attaching large methods inside constructors (this.method = fn), which re-allocates a new function for every single instance.
Using '__proto__' directly in production code; use Object.getPrototypeOf() and Object.create() instead.

sections.heading: 2. Production-Grade EventEmitter with Memory-Efficient Delegation
sections.content: Node.js and modern frontend architectures are driven by event emitters. Defining event dispatch methods on the class prototype ensures thousands of concurrent socket connections share identical method pointers in memory.

codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates high-performance prototype delegation, private class fields (#events), and defensive listener execution.

keyPoints: Using Set for listener storage prevents duplicate listener registrations.
Returning a cleanup function from on() simplifies unsubscribe logic in UI frameworks.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to iterate over a copy of listeners ([...listeners]); removing listeners during emit causes off-by-one skipping.

exercises.title: Implement an Authenticated User Entity with Role Delegation
exercises.objective: Create User and Admin classes using ES6 inheritance with encapsulated password hash fields.
exercises.description: Build a User class with username and a private #passwordHash. Provide a verifyPassword(pwd) method. Create an Admin subclass that inherits from User, adds a permissions array, and overrides a toJSON() method that safely omits private hashes.
instructions: Extend User into Admin and add hasPermission(perm) method.
Ensure JSON.stringify(admin) never exposes the password hash.
hints: Use `#passwordHash;` at the top of the User class.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Private fields (#) are hard boundaries enforced by the V8 runtime, preventing reflection or enumeration leaks.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is the primary memory advantage of defining methods on a class prototype rather than inside the constructor?

options.text: Prototype methods run in Web Workers automatically.
Prototype methods exist as a single shared function in memory across all instances, rather than being re-created for each instance.
Prototype methods bypass garbage collection entirely.
Prototype methods can only be invoked asynchronously.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Methods on the prototype are allocated once in memory. All instances delegate to this shared object, saving massive RAM.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: How are private class fields (e.g. #apiKey) enforced in modern JavaScript?

options.text: Through a naming convention that developers agree to respect.
By the V8 JavaScript engine itself at compile and runtime; attempting to access outside the class throws a SyntaxError.
By automatically converting the property into a symbol.
By freezing the object using Object.freeze().

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Native private fields (#) are hard private variables enforced directly by the JavaScript runtime engine.

recap: JavaScript uses prototype delegation for inheritance. ES6 classes provide clean syntax with native private fields (#) and memory-efficient shared methods.
